item.title: Singapore’s Top Envoy Visits Indonesia After Natural Gas Cuts
item.description: Singapore Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan is scheduled to meet his Indonesian counterpart in Jakarta on Tuesday, days after Indonesia trimmed natural gas exports to the city-state.
item.dc:creator: Chandra Asmara

item.title: Toronto Reelects Chow as Mayor on Affordability Pledges
item.description: Toronto reelected its progressive mayor, Olivia Chow, for a second term on Monday, opting to stick with her agenda of stronger social services and improved affordability.
item.dc:creator: Melissa Shin and Monique Mulima

item.title: Trump Rallies in Mississippi With Republican Senate Seat at Risk
item.description: President Donald Trump urged Republican voters to head to the polls during a campaign rally in deep-red Mississippi, saying he couldn’t “take a chance” of Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith losing her seat.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Subramanian

item.title: Bolsonaro Backs Off Election Challenge as His Party Concedes
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro abandoned plans to challenge the result of Brazil’s presidential election, while his Liberal Party went a step further and formally conceded defeat to reelected President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Carvalho

item.title: New DOJ Charges Against Ex-FBI Chief Comey Unsealed by Court
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Keisha Lance Bottoms, Georgia's Democratic gubernatorial candidate, in a pre-recorded interview, says she wants to pause new data center construction while the state examines the industry's impact on the electric grid, consumer costs, public health and water supplies. Mark Esper, former Defense Secretary and Partner at Red Cell Ventures, says he does not see the benefit of a US attack on Iran and says the economic blockade is working. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: Anthropic Files for IPO (Podcast)
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
Anthropic filed for its IPO and expects to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT. The company's IPO will serve as a litmus test for investor demand for new equity tied to the AI trade, and its debut has become a focal point for hopes and fears over artificial intelligence. Anthropic's prospectus flagged various "risks to humanity" including attempts to "resist shutdown" and "conceal or manipulate information," and the company emphasized the potential for its AI to "behave in unintended, misaligned, or autonomous ways."
On today's episode:
Shirin Ghaffary, Bloomberg News AI Reporter Rudina Seseri, Founder and Managing Partner at Glasswing Ventures Axel Merk, President and Chief Investment Officer, Merk Investments Dave Lee, Bloomberg Opinion US Technology Columnist (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: DOJ Bid for Fast Ruling in California Voting Case Rejected
item.description: The Trump administration on Monday struck out in its attempt to rapidly block California from counting 20,000 mail-in ballots from people it says are “likely” non-citizens, though the fight may still be far from over.
item.dc:creator: Erik Larson

item.title: Bottoms Says Georgia Needs Pause on New Data Centers
item.description: Keisha Lance Bottoms, Georgia's Democratic gubernatorial candidate, in a pre-recorded interview, says she wants to pause new data center construction while the state examines the industry's impact on the electric grid, consumer costs, public health and water supplies. Bottoms says the pause could last from one month to six months or longer and says the state should determine whether Georgia needs additional data centers and how to allow future development responsibly. Bottoms says Georgia should expand Medicaid, arguing that 300,000 people lack health insurance coverage because the state has not done so and that nine rural hospitals have closed. Bottoms says she supports responsible, lawful immigration enforcement, but opposes tactics she thinks are disruptive to communities and local law enforcement. She speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: DOJ Accuses Ex-FBI Director Comey of Sharing Defense Secrets
item.description: The US Justice Department accused former FBI Director James Comey of illegally directing the sharing of secret national defense information 10 years ago, according to a court filing unsealed on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Chris Strohm

item.title: Anthropic IPO, AI Financing & Markets Rally
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Russell Investments President & CIO Kate El-Hillow, Harbor Capital Advisors Portfolio Manager Justin Menne, ValueEdge Advisors Chair Nell Minow, Strategic Value Partners Founder & CIO Victor Khosla, Moderna CEO Stéphane Bancel, Barclays Head of US Equity Strategy, Global Equity Linked Strategies Venu Krishna, The IPO Initiative Director Jay Ritter, Willow Wealth CEO Mitch Caplan, Duke’s Mayo Company E. Yuri Hermida, Once Upon a Farm Co-Founder & Chief Brand Officer Jennifer Garner, & Edward Jones Head of Policy, Regulatory & Government Relations Andy Blocker. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: This Election Is About Voters’ Pocketbooks: Andy Blocker
item.description: Andy Blocker, Head of Policy, Regulatory and Government Relations at Edward Jones, says voters are focused less on broad economic indicators and market performance than on whether they can cover current bills and save for retirement. He describes the election as being about “green” in voters’ pockets and says the outcome remains uncertain despite predictions that it is settled. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Affordability Weighs Heavily on Voters for Midterms
item.description: Bloomberg’s Mark Niquette says voters who shifted toward Trump in 2024—including young, low-income and Latino voters—are increasingly frustrated with the economy and feel he has not kept his promise to lower prices. He co-wrote The Big Take and reports on "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US-Canada Trade Talks Are Picking Up Pace But No Deal Yet, Carney Says
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said trade talks with the US have gained a bit of momentum, and suggested that any progress has been because the Trump administration has shown more flexibility.
item.dc:creator: Nojoud Al Mallees

item.title: US Maps Path for Venezuela to Hold Fresh Presidential Election
item.description: Venezuela and the US are setting up a path toward elections in the South American country that would be triggered by declaring a vacancy in the office, which technically has been empty since American forces captured Nicolás Maduro in January.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Laya and Magdalena Del Valle

item.title: NY’s MTA Faces $95.6 Million Fuel Hit This Year From Iran War
item.description: New York’s Metropolitan Transportation Authority, the largest mass-transit provider in the US, anticipates paying an additional $95.6 million for fuel this year after the war in Iran disrupted oil supplies and sent prices soaring.
item.dc:creator: Michelle Kaske

item.title: Does France Answer to Its Citizens or the Bond Market?
item.description: France’s budget battle is testing two powerful forces: citizens who want to see the social safety net maintained and even expanded and a bond market that can’t stomach the idea of France’s deficit getting any larger. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Says Brazil Election Looked ‘Rigged’ After Lula’s Win
item.description: US President Donald Trump said Brazil’s runoff election looked “rigged,” after that country’s president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, pulled off a stunning comeback victory against challenger Flávio Bolsonaro.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Subramanian, Hadriana Lowenkron and Daniel Carvalho

item.title: Trump Rushes to Defend Red State of Mississippi
item.description: Jim Kessler, executive vice president for Policy at Third Way, said that the organization's polling shows that voters are moving away from Donald Trump and toward Democrats and that the upcoming midterm elections feel like not only a blue wave, but a 'blue tidal wave.' Kessler said that he sees a path for Democrats to take the Senate and pick up as many as 54 seats if they win longshot races in Iowa and Kansas. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: UK Set to Raise Pay Floor 4% as Burnham Seeks Cost of Living Fix
item.description: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey is poised to raise the UK’s national living wage by about 4%, but will not close the pay gap with younger workers, amid growing concern that hiring costs are driving youth unemployment.
item.dc:creator: Philip Aldrick and Chloe Chaplain

item.title: Milei Is Lone South American Leader Yet to Accept Lula’s Win
item.description: Argentine President Javier Milei was the only South American leader on Monday who hasn’t yet recognized Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s victory in Brazil’s election, diverging from his allies in the region.
item.dc:creator: Manuela Tobias
